chapter_theme: The eight great siddhis (அட்டமா சித்தி): powers such as becoming minute, light, heavy or all-pervading, and entering another body, said to come by eightfold yoga, by holding the breath in the central channel and by a year's union with a form of Shakti. The chapter frames them with grace: the siddhis come when Shakti grants them, the Lord who cuts off birth gives them, and walking the world finds nothing that love does not.
structure_note: The verses fall into loose groups: the siddhis as the Lord's gift (640 to 643); powers listed by years of practice (644 to 652); the ten vital airs, chiefly dhananjaya, and the diseases of their disorder (653 to 658); the central channel, nada and the Lady in the lotus stalk (659 to 667); the eight siddhis one by one, each reached in a year with a named Lady (668 to 693); breath counts for each Lady (694 to 703); and a close on samadhi, a list of twenty-one powers, love over pilgrimage, and freedom from death (704 to 711).

640.reading: Bowing and seeking the Supreme in all eight directions, worshipping our Lord there with resolve, the eight great siddhis were established in the eight directions.
640.nuance: எண் திசை (eight directions) repeats in every line, matching the eight siddhis. Who established them, and what தணிந்து (calmed, subdued) qualifies, is unclear; the verse may be the poet's own account of how he received them.

641.reading: Seeking without fault the feet of the Lord whose nature the gods know, I saw the pure space; the eight great siddhis are not hard for me, for he gave great grace and cut off my birth.
641.nuance: தூவெளி (pure space) is a yogic term for the open expanse of awareness, as tradition takes it. The verse sets the siddhis beside the cutting of birth, and credits both to grace rather than to technique.

642.reading: By the guru's grace, Mular, following the sign, looked to the fragrant ... of Parai; with the shambhavi and khechari seals joined, the great Siva-state is the gain of the eight siddhis.
642.nuance: சாம்பவி and கேசரி are names of yogic seals (mudras), traditionally the inward gaze and the tongue turned back. சங்கட்டம் is obscure; a variant reads சக்கட்டம், perhaps the wheel or circle. The verse names the author, Mular.

643.reading: If the one beginningless knowledge, which body, elements, kala, time and maya cannot reach, joins the truth of the unceasing Lord, entering another's body becomes possible.
643.nuance: காயாதி பூதம் கலை காலம் மாயை lists tattvas from the body up to maya. பரகாயம் is usually entering another's body; it can also be read as the supreme body. ஆயாது அகல is unclear: 'parting without being examined' or 'separating without being caught'.

644.reading: The twenty thousand eight hundred kinds of karma, mantra and yoga only give the body toil; for siddhi they come down to four.
644.nuance: The number and the four (a variant has அருமிரு, two) are not explained. The plain point is that many practices reduce to a few that matter.

645.reading: Of the kalas that abide as twelve in the moon, when the rising of four is gone and eight remain, if one looks without attachment for twelve years, twelve firm siddhis arise.
645.nuance: The moon's kalas are a figure for the breath and the inner moon in yogic reading; the arithmetic of twelve, four and eight is obscure. The twelve years open the sequence of powers by year in 646 to 648.

646.reading: Powers that come in order with the years: freedom when disease and poison surround, arts and learning, long intellect and keen wisdom, ... and hearing from afar, ending at the twelfth.
646.nuance: The verse is a compressed list and its grammar is hard to follow; பீடொன்றினால் வாயா is unclear. The list overlaps with the powers in 705 and 706.

647.reading: In the seventh year one has the speed of a storm wind, an untiring pace that covers many yojanas; in the eighth grey hair and wrinkles do not appear; in the ninth comes entering another's body.
647.nuance: The years are supplied from the ordinals (ஏழு, எட்டு, ஒன்பது) and the context of 645; they may count stages rather than years. நரைதிரை, grey hair and wrinkles, is the standard pair for old age.

648.reading: In the tenth one is filled and becomes Rudra in meditation; in the eleventh the eight siddhis; and going through the seven worlds above and seven below, standing all-pervading, comes in the twelfth.
648.nuance: The first word of lines 2 to 4 varies across copies (ஏர்வொன்று, நேரொன்று, ஓரொன்று), and the line division of years is uncertain.

649.reading: The eight are: becoming atomic, lightness in the world, unyielding heaviness, the body entering another body, becoming whatever one wills, the nature of joining the supreme body, unfailing truth, and pervading all.
649.nuance: The standard eight are anima, mahima, laghima, garima, prapti, prakamya, ishitva and vashitva. The verse's list does not map onto them cleanly, and variants (நோன்மையும், ககனமும்) change two items.

650.reading: Holding all things, becoming atomic, drawing many lives in, there is no further lack; rising within those from which we rose and growing high is how the boon of release came first.
650.nuance: The syntax is loose and the variant கோண்கிய வாமுத்தி is garbled. One reading is that the powers rest on release; another that release is reached through them.

651.reading: The former three hundred and sixty measures of time came as nazhigai beginning from space; as one meditates again and again, discerning from earth upward, it rises from the navel.
651.nuance: முந்நூற்றறுபது (360) may count days, breaths or units of time; நாழிகை is a unit of twenty-four minutes. மண்முதல் (from earth) suggests meditating the elements in order, and உந்தி (navel) the seat from which the breath rises.

652.reading: Those whose mind turns and becomes full of Siva, who have discerned release and reached silence, are freed in Siva; free of the five bonds they gain purity, their mind in the Supreme, in the holy dance.
652.nuance: சிவமுத்தர் (those freed in Siva) and மோனர் (the silent) name a state beyond the powers just listed. ஐந்தில் தொடக்கு, bond in the five, may be the five senses or a fivefold count of malas; the verse does not say.

653.reading: These nine vital airs are in accord; above them is dhananjaya; while it stays in accord within the nine, body and life stay together.
653.nuance: The tradition counts ten airs (prana, apana, vyana, udana, samana, naga, kurma, krikara, devadatta, dhananjaya). The verse makes dhananjaya the tenth and the one on which body and life hold together.

654.reading: Dhananjaya stays in the nine airs, as two hundred and twenty-three; if it does not stay in the body, the body swells and bursts.
654.nuance: இருநூற்றிருபத்து மூன்று (223) is not explained. Dhananjaya is traditionally the air that swells the corpse after death; here its failure in the living body causes swelling.

655.reading: Swellings, tumours, scabies and leprosy, many swelling diseases and anaemia, swollen wind-disease, hunchback and lameness, and diseases settling in the eye.
655.nuance: The verse continues 654: these are the diseases of a disordered dhananjaya. வீங்கு (swell) opens every line.

656.reading: Eye disease comes from dhananjaya, cough does not; because kurma is not mixed in the eye, the light is not mixed in the eye either.
656.nuance: Kurma is traditionally the air that moves the eyelids. இவ்வாணிகள் is obscure, and the logic of the last two lines (no kurma, so no light) is unclear.

657.reading: Isa among the gods, Tirumal and Brahma stood there without ceasing and knew the radiant light that reaches through the sound in the channel, the eye and the heart.
657.nuance: நாடியின் ஓசை (the sound in the channel) and தூடி அளவு are obscure; தூடி may be a measure or a misreading. The point seems to be that even the gods reached this inner light by stillness.

658.reading: In the body with nine gates is one place with nine channels; for those who can still the nine channels, the nine visions ... become many.
658.nuance: The nine gates are the body's openings. The last line, ஒன்பது காட்சி இலை பல ஆமே, can be read 'the nine visions are not; many come', and a variant has உலைநலம் ஆமே. I can't fix it.

659.reading: When the bright sushumna runs below the rising fire, drawing in, and the sun and moon run their way, holding up and bearing the seven worlds: this we told to those on the rare path.
659.nuance: இரவி மதி (sun and moon) are taken in yoga as the right and left channels, pingala and ida; the fire below as the fire at the root where kundalini lies. The seven worlds may be the body's centres.

660.reading: As the Lord, meeting her, sought the Lady, like a doe caught in a net of bonds, if one makes the balanced channel a pure path it becomes a seed set aside to be sold.
660.nuance: துலைப்பட்ட நாடி, the channel that is balanced like a scale, is taken as the central channel between ida and pingala. The doe in the net and the seed kept for sale are images I can't place with confidence.

661.reading: Those who ran there and saw the one thing raise nada within the channel; seeking there, they scoop up honey and drink it, and bind the enemies who stood in the camp.
661.nuance: பாடி (camp) is taken as the body, the enemies as the senses or passions, and the honey as the inner nectar. The plain image is of a raid that ends in a feast and a binding.

662.reading: In the stalk of the bound lotus nine adorned maidens joined the Lady; standing bound, passing through the dark fruit and standing at the brow-mark, it became full.
662.nuance: The lotus stalk is taken as the central channel and the nine maidens as nine shaktis. களங்கனி (the dark kalam fruit) and பொட்டு (the brow-mark) may be centres at the throat or palate and the brow. The variants in line 3 are garbled.

663.reading: The full Shakti, divided as seven and three, and the beautiful maidens who made seven hundred and five, became the cause of the five beginning with Narayana and Brahma, and mingled and spread.
663.nuance: The five gods are traditionally the agents of the five acts. The numbers (ஏழுமூன்று, எழுநூற்றஞ்சு) are not explained.

664.reading: If this Lady, who expanded, contracted and ripened, rises hidden within and stays hidden there, the elements from earth that spread out are drawn in, and the roaring breath subsides in its place.
664.nuance: The Lady (மங்கை) may be Shakti as kundalini. விரிந்து குவிந்து (expanding and contracting) suits both the cosmos and the breath.

665.reading: The two airs called ida and pingala, flowing through their channels, stand reversed; their hindrances, six and seven, subside in the lightning creeper that grows in the cool light.
665.nuance: மின்கொடி, the lightning creeper, is a common figure for kundalini or the central channel. ஆறேழு may be six and seven, or forty-two; a variant reads ஆறு எழும், the six that rise.

666.reading: If one stills and gathers oneself and stays aware there, the breath folds and subsides within; folding within the abiding life, the dancer who took up the dance seeks him.
666.nuance: In the text the dancer (Siva) seeks the stilled one; the variant கூத்தனை நாடுகின்றேனே reverses this to 'I seek the dancer'. The reversal changes who moves first.

667.reading: Seeking within the channel with the sound of nada, going and taking hold of that sacred one, binding the enemies in the camp, it became a jewelled lamp in one hand.
667.nuance: Line 3 repeats 661. திரு (the sacred, Shri) may be Shakti. மாடி ஒருகை is obscure; the lamp in the hand suggests a light that is now one's own.

668.reading: To name the siddhis beginning with anima: being an atom within the atom, greatness, lightness, unbending weight, entering another body, and being everywhere though an atom: these are the eight.
668.nuance: This list is closer to the standard eight than 649's, but the mapping of each phrase is still uncertain: நேர்மை and இணுகாத ஏகார் are hard to fix.

669.reading: The eight siddhis come through eightfold yoga, by mastering the prana that is hard to master; when the fire at the root of the central channel drives the sun and lets the moon drink, the higher ones come too.
669.nuance: எட்டி யோகம, eightfold yoga, is the limbs of yoga from restraints to samadhi. The fire, sun and moon are the usual yogic figures for the root fire and the right and left channels.

670.reading: Through eightfold yoga, beyond the eight siddhis, all kinds of understanding become clear; the siddhis, the eight, come into being when Shakti Tripurai grants grace.
670.nuance: The verse puts the siddhis under Shakti's grace, not under the practice alone, and places understanding (புத்தி) above them.

671.reading: Those who have gained these eight with the beautiful Supreme are siddhas, since they reach the supreme world; holding firm within what they love is the supreme vision, and the eight boundaries reach to where he stands.
671.nuance: சித்தர் is defined here by reaching the supreme world, not by the powers alone. The last line is obscure; the variant இருக்கல் (staying) for இறுக்கல் (holding tight) changes little.

672.reading: For those who can reverse the moon and sun that climb the mountain and be free of dross in the pit like a bulb, the good world of desire is reached without effort; that world is anima and the rest.
672.nuance: மந்தரம் (the mountain) may be the spine; குழி (the pit) the root centre; கந்து, a bulb or post. The variant காய மிய for கா மிய changes 'world of desire' to something about the body.

673.reading: Binding it and practising for a year, he becomes the anima he puts on; lighter than carded cotton, he stays thin and cannot be overcome.
673.nuance: The lightness of cotton suits laghima more than anima. முடிந்திட்டு வைத்து (binding and setting) is taken as holding the breath.

674.reading: With that singular Lady who arises, the tattvas that go everywhere become a refuge; if the times of dying stay in one's own control, in five years comes great lightness.
674.nuance: மாலகு is taken as great lightness (laghima). மாய்கின்றது ஐயாண்டின் might also mean 'what dies in five years'. The formula 'with the Lady' recurs through 694 to 702.

675.reading: After seeing the wondrous one who has become great lightness, he stays flourishing as light; it stood spread everywhere as milk-white light, and he sees the true thing that is the higher light.
675.nuance: மாயன் can mean Vishnu, the wondrous one, or the illusory; who becomes light (the yogi or the seen) is unclear.

676.reading: When one's own tattva joins the gentle Lady who spoke the truth and mingles with it like a thing held in the hand, in a year one becomes the dark thing, mahima.
676.nuance: மகிமா (greatness) is one of the eight. மைப்பொருள் (the dark or black thing) is obscure.

677.reading: After seeing the light of the breath that rises, the passing times no longer pass; the time above stood open in space, and the times that remain go one's own way.
677.nuance: கால் means both breath and time, and the verse plays on the two: mastering the breath is mastering time. 680 repeats much of it.

678.reading: Knowledge flourishes as his way, the world flourishes as his way, all things flourish as his way; he stands as his own way, as his own grace.
678.nuance: தான் may be the Lord or the yogi who has gained the powers; the second fits the chapter, the first the closing words தன்னருள். Line 1 is garbled in the source (ஞ்aனமும், read as ஞானமும்).

679.reading: If one stays a year with the Lady of the tattvas, holding all the hosts of elements one has seen, what opens is good prapti.
679.nuance: பிராத்தி is prapti, the power of reaching anything. The formula of a year with a Lady recurs in 682 and 684.

680.reading: After seeing the light of lightning that rises, one can see the spreading worlds in the ripening flower; the moving time stood open in space, and the passing times do not pass.
680.nuance: Lines 3 and 4 repeat 677. The flower (பூ) may be a lotus centre or the earth.

681.reading: For those who know, there is nothing that goes, nothing that comes, nothing that dies, nothing that grows, no delay, and no light at all in the inner cave.
681.nuance: தமரகம் is the small inner cavity, traditionally of the heart or head. After the verses on seeing lights, this one denies even light: the knower's state is beyond change, and beyond the visions too.

682.reading: If one dwells within the known Parashakti, the hosts of elements fall away; if one stays a year with them gathered, entering another's body becomes possible.
682.nuance: The formula follows 679 and 684. பரகாயம் மேவல் recurs from 643.

683.reading: People do not know what the lamp's light is; for those who already have the light of the root lamp and see the light of the lamp that is seen, the light of the higher lamp makes release easy.
683.nuance: The four lamps (ஆன, மூல, கான, மேலை) may be stages of an inner light rising from the root centre to the crown, as tradition takes them. கான may be 'seen' or 'of the forest'.

684.reading: If one stays a year with the Lady of Sadasiva, gathering all the hosts of elements one has seen, one becomes the ancient Lord's tattva.
684.nuance: ஈசன் தத்துவம், the Lord's tattva, is taken as ishitva, lordship, one of the eight.

685.reading: He becomes the light of the rising moon and its coolness; if the moon's kala joins, he becomes the moon itself.
685.nuance: The moon is a yogic figure for the cool nectar in the head. ஆகின்ற சந்திரன் opens every line. A variant reads தண்ணளி, cool grace.

686.reading: He becomes able to create, able to protect, and lord of destruction; he becomes one of whom it is said, he is himself the one.
686.nuance: In context the subject is the yogi who has gained ishitva, taking on the Lord's acts. The verse names three acts, not the five, and does not say whether the yogi becomes the Lord or only acts like him.

687.reading: If, within the kala that flourished in its nature, one firmly turns back the five elements spread out in many forms, in a year one sees the subtle true thing.
687.nuance: மறித்திடில் (turning back) suggests withdrawing the elements into their source. The verse plays on தன்மை, பன்மை, வன்மை, மென்மை.

688.reading: If you ask what ripened as the true thing, it is the good vashitva; he becomes the very self of all lives, mingled with them like a thing in hand.
688.nuance: வசித்துவம் is vashitva, the power of bringing beings under one's will. The verse turns it into being the self of all lives, a gentler sense than control.

689.reading: If the sun that flourished in its nature sees the subtle true thing, and the senses become golden and go, one sees the good creeper.
689.nuance: The creeper (கொடி) is a figure for Shakti or kundalini, and the sun for the right channel. பொன்மையதாக (becoming golden) is obscure.

690.reading: If one knows the body of that creeper with the Lady who is the good creeper, in a year one goes to the golden worlds and returns, and becomes the lover of the stone creeper.
690.nuance: காமுகன் (lover, one who desires) may point to the power of having one's desires fulfilled (prakamya). கற்கொடி, the stone creeper, is obscure.

691.reading: After the lovely tattva comes, the fragrance of the flower becomes the world; ... the light where the tongue dwells becomes lordship.
691.nuance: Line 3 is obscure, and a variant reads உன்னிடம் எய்திடு, 'reaching your place'. நா (the tongue) may refer to the tongue turned back in khechari.

692.reading: After seeing the good light that is lordship, it stays flourishing as a mother's home; after seeing the worlds that went within, one sees the great light.
692.nuance: பேயகம் is obscure, perhaps the cremation ground where Siva dances, or the great void.

693.reading: He who has seen with trembling that great ... which is the great light, as the light of the earth, sees the light of the breath, the one light that is the whole earth as a garland of light.
693.nuance: வேட்டை (hunt) does not fit; the variant வெட்டை (open space, void) fits better. காலொளி, the breath's light, recurs from 677.

694.reading: To tell how breath and life mingle: the breath is with that creeper Lady, and it is wanted in five hundred and thirteen, in this way.
694.nuance: 694 to 703 give breath counts for a series of Ladies or kalas. The numbers are not explained, and a variant in line 4 (பெண்மண்டி) is garbled.

695.reading: Six is in the head of nectar; six is a thousand three hundred and five; six becomes a thousand on the rare path; what grows as six is two.
695.nuance: ஆறு means both six and path, and the verse may play on both. The counts are obscure.

696.reading: Above the two is the Lady of Sadasiva; to tell how the two rise taking breath, two thousand and fifty-one gathered, and the time taken is five.
696.nuance: The numbers are not explained; கால் is again both breath and time.

697.reading: The Lady with five and five faces: five with five is ayuta; besides that five, two thousand; the time taken is one.
697.nuance: அஞ்சுடன் அஞ்சு முகம் (five and five faces) may be the ten faces of a goddess. ஆயுதம் may be ayuta (ten thousand) or 'weapon'.

698.reading: The Lady of the tattva that is one: to tell how the one moves taking breath, the one wins thousands upon thousands, and the time taken is before.
698.nuance: ஒன்று opens every line; the counts are obscure.

699.reading: With the Lady of that kala who rises first, the measure where the breath ends is fifty-one with five.
699.nuance: Fifty-one may be the letters of the Sanskrit alphabet, which mantra theory links to the kalas; the verse doesn't say so.

700.reading: With that singular Lady hard to fathom, the measure of breath is five hundred and thirty-nine, and the breath stayed within its measure.
700.nuance: ஆய்வரும் (hard to examine) opens each line. மாய்வரு வாயு may be 'the breath that ends' or 'the wondrous breath'.

701.reading: In the Father who is the twofold treasure, the way the breath moves is two hundred and thirty-three with five: these are the letters in which the breath moves.
701.nuance: இருநிதி (twofold treasure) is obscure; எழுத்து (letter) suggests the counts are of syllables in a mantra or breaths matched to letters.

702.reading: With the Lady in the rising light, the place of the breath is seven hundred and twenty-nine and four, and the fire rose and stayed with it in this way.
702.nuance: The fire (அங்கி) may be the root fire of 659 and 669. The counts are obscure.

703.reading: Taking six breaths it produces essence; taking seven it doubles and brings it down; taking eight the places come into accord; and with nine the breath is even across the great ground.
703.nuance: இரதம் may be rasa, the bodily essence or nectar. The verse reads like a practice of breath counts, but its terms can't be fixed.

704.reading: The yogi of the light of samadhi sees at the juncture how the moon meets sun, Supreme and Sthanu, and becomes one with the world.
704.nuance: சந்தி (juncture) may be the meeting of the channels or the twilight hour. தாணு (the pillar) is a name of Siva. சகமுகத்து உந்தி is obscure.

705.reading: A list of powers: freedom from afflicting spirits, removing poison, learning that is revered and great wisdom, ... hearing from afar, becoming invisible, and moving with the speed of wind.
705.nuance: அணங்கு is an afflicting spirit or goddess; அருஞ்சனம் may be poison or a rare collyrium. Line 3 is garbled in a variant. The list repeats much of 646.

706.reading: Escaping death and old age, entering another's body, giving the earth of battle to the dead, and gaining the form of Hara: one who has learned the count knows these as three sevens.
706.nuance: மூவேழ் (three sevens, twenty-one) closes the list begun in 705. சரைவிடல் (leaving old age) has a variant சிறைவிடல் (release from prison). Line 2 is obscure.

707.reading: Circling the world where the sea roars and walking till the feet ache is of no use; those sweet ones who see the Lord in love know the city where the Lord dwells.
707.nuance: The verse sets love (காதல்) against pilgrimage. The city (நகர்) is not named; tradition reads it as the body or the heart. Placed in a chapter on powers, it may also say that travel to the worlds, a siddhi, is not the point.

708.reading: With the root, the first one, Brahma, Vishnu and Hara before him, as the five-faced one declares: supreme bindu, ample supreme nada, bindu, the single nada, the sheltering Shakti and Parai are the feet of the Supreme.
708.nuance: The five-faced one is Sadasiva. The list of bindu, nada, Shakti and Parai follows the stages of Saiva cosmology, as in chapter 140; how they divide is unclear.

709.reading: Going with the deity of adhara yoga, with Parai above, joining the Supreme, as the sixteen kalas from medha rise, the light above, unspoken and unthinkable, is the yoga of bliss.
709.nuance: ஆதார யோகம் is yoga through the body's centres. மேதாதி ஈரெண் கலை, the sixteen kalas beginning with medha, are a mantra-theory series. ஆனந்த யோகம், the yoga of bliss, is the chapter's goal beyond the powers.

710.reading: When moon and sun come and join, the ancient gods praise; to the true devotees who do what is ordained, the Supreme stands and shows the Lord.
710.nuance: பதி may be the Lord, the Pati of Siddhanta, or the place (abode). Moon and sun meeting is again the joining of the side channels.

711.reading: Those who pierce till the brow-spot rises, plant the staff till sparks rise, and know, have no Yama; those who can bind become hidden and are everywhere, wedded within the honey-opening lotus.
711.nuance: பொட்டு (brow-spot), தண்டு (staff, taken as the spine) and பொறி (sparks) are yogic figures. நமனில்லை (no Yama) can mean freedom from death or from death's power over the soul, and the two readings differ greatly.

links.note: Both say a discipline can carry one past Death: the Kural's power gained through tapas leaps over Yama (கூற்றம் குதித்தல்); Tirumular's yogis of the brow and staff have no Yama (நமனில்லை).

The Naladiyar says no one has leapt clear of Death and escaped, so give while you can; Tirumular says those who know the yogic way have no Yama. The conflict holds if நமனில்லை means escape from bodily death; if it means freedom from Yama's judgement after death, the two need not clash.

The Naladiyar's wise renounce in childhood because grey hair will surely come; Tirumular says that by the eighth stage of practice grey hair and wrinkles do not appear. The conflict depends on reading 647 literally, as a claim about the body, and not as a figure for inner freshness.

Both say not every lamp is the lamp: the Kural's one true lamp is truthfulness, Tirumular's is the higher inner light that makes release easy. The image is shared, the light is moral in one and yogic in the other.
669 says the eight siddhis come by eightfold yoga and mastered breath; 670 adds that they come into being only when Shakti Tripurai grants grace. Technique is necessary but not sufficient.
Two lists of the eight siddhis in one chapter. 668's is closer to the standard anima list; set side by side they show the items were not fixed in wording.
641 credits the siddhis and the end of birth to grace given to one who sought the Lord's feet; 707 says outward travel finds nothing, and love alone knows where the Lord dwells.

640 says that bowing and worshipping the Lord in the eight directions (தொழுதெம் பிரானை) set the eight great siddhis in place. 1006 says that if one comes and worships (எய்தி வழிப்படில்) the eight siddhis come (எண்சித்தி உண்டாகும்), after Indra's wealth and before release. Both make the siddhis a fruit of worship, and 1006 shows they are a middle stage, not the end.

641 says the eight great siddhis are not hard for him (அரியது எனக்கில்லை அட்டமா சித்தி) because the Lord gave grace and cut off his birth. Thiruppugazh 281 asks to be set at the red-gold feet that make all powers and the eight siddhis easy (அகில சத்தியும் எட்டுறு சித்தியும் எளிதென). In both the siddhis become easy through the Lord's gift and stand second to the release or the feet asked for.

642 says that by the guru's grace, with the shambhavi and khechari seals joined (சாம்பவி கேசரி சேர), the great Siva-state is the gain of the eight siddhis. 1897 names the yoga mudra as the eight siddhis (யோகத்தின் முத்திரை ஓர்அட்ட சித்தியாம்) and sorts khechari and shambhavi between yoga and knowledge. The pairing shows the two seals tied to the siddhis in both places, with 1897 setting them under separate paths.

643 speaks of one beginningless knowledge (அறிவொன்று அனாதியே) that body, elements, kala, time and maya do not reach, and makes entering another body possible when it joins the Lord. 2181 says the thirty-six tattvas are without knowledge (அறிவொன்றிலாதன) and that he learned from Nandi that he himself is the knower. 2181 says what 643's knowledge apart from the tattvas is: the soul as knower, made known by the guru.

643 says that when the beginningless knowledge joins the Lord, entering another body (பரகாயம் மேவல்) becomes possible. 1906 says the faultless jnani-yogi, leaving the body, becomes That and does not take another body (பரகாயம் சாராதே). Read together, the power 643 promises is one the perfected knower of 1906 no longer uses.

644 says twenty thousand eight hundred kinds of karma, mantra and yoga only tire the body (காய உழைப்பாகும்), and for siddhi they come down to four. Naladiyar 135 says learning has no shore and life is short, so learn what is fitting, like the bird that leaves the water and drinks the milk. Both answer a boundless stock of means with the same move, reducing it to the few that serve the end.

646 lists powers that come in order: freedom from disease and poison, arts and learning, long intellect and keen wisdom (கலைகல்வி நீள்மேதை கூர்ஞானம்), hearing from afar. 705 repeats the same items: removing poison, revered learning and great wisdom (வணங்குற்ற கல்விமா ஞானம்), hearing from afar (தூரங் கேட்டல்). The near-repeat shows the chapter counting learning and wisdom among the siddhis, not only as their means.

652 says those whose mind becomes full of Siva and who have reached silence (மோனர்) are freed in Siva (சிவமுத்தர்). 1611 says that for those to whom silence has come (மோனங்கை வந்தோர்க்கு) release comes and the siddhis stand before them. Both put silence and release above the powers this chapter lists; 1611 adds that the powers then follow of themselves.

653 says the nine airs are in accord (ஒத்த) with dhananjaya above them, and while it stays in accord body and life stay together; 654 and 655 list the swellings that follow when it does not. Kural 941 says the three humours beginning with wind (வளிமுதலா எண்ணிய மூன்று) cause disease whether in excess or deficiency. Yogic and medical texts share one logic: health is the balance of the body's airs or humours, disease their disorder.

655 lists swellings, tumour (கழலை), leprosy and anaemia (சோகை) as diseases of a disordered dhananjaya. 263 gives anaemia (சோகை) and tumour (கழலை) a moral cause: they come to those who do not do dharma and stay away from those who do. Set side by side, the same diseases get a bodily cause in 655 and a moral one in 263, and neither verse mentions the other's.

657 says Isa, Tirumal and Brahma stood without ceasing and knew (உணர்ந்திருந்தாரே) the radiant light reached through the sound in the channel. 88 says Brahma and Vishnu, seeking foot and crown, did not see his form (படிகண்டிலர்), and Brahma lied that he had. The conflict holds if 657's light is the same Lord 88 calls unseen; if it is an inner yogic light, 657 may be saying that stillness found what the search of 88 missed.

658 places in the body of nine gates (ஒன்பது வாசல்) a place of nine channels, and those who still them gain visions. Naladiyar 47 calls the body a pot that seeps filth from nine openings (ஒன்பது வாய்ப்புலனும்) to shame the lover. The same nine openings are a cause for disgust in the Naladiyar and a site of practice in Tirumular.

658 speaks of the body with nine gates (ஒன்பது வாசல்) holding nine channels that can be stilled. 470 says the Lord set the body with nine gates as sluices (மடைவைத்த ஒன்பது வாய்தலும்) and set fire at the lotus of the head. Both treat the nine openings as built for a purpose, and 470 names the builder.

661 says those who ran and saw the one thing raise nada within the channel (நாடியி னுள்ளாக நாதம் எழுப்புவர்), drink the honey and bind the enemies in the camp. 667 repeats the line on binding the enemies in the camp (பாடியுள் நின்ற பகைவரைக் கட்டிட்டு) after seeking with the sound of nada in the channel, and ends in a jewelled lamp. It is a near-repeat inside the chapter; 667 gives the end as light where 661 gives it as honey.

667 ends the inner search with the nada in the channel as a jewelled lamp in one hand (மணிவிளக் கானதே). 820 says that when the breath rises the temple daubed with black, the body, becomes a jewelled lamp (மையணி கோயில் மணிவிளக் காமே). Both use the gem lamp for the light that held breath and inner sound kindle in the body.

669 says the eight siddhis come by eightfold yoga and mastered breath, when the fire at the root of the central channel (நடுநாடி மூலத்த னல்) drives the sun and lets the moon drink. Thiruppugazh 1045 describes the breath stopped, the fire kindled at the root (மூல ... அனல்மூள) and the nectar drunk, with the powers of striking Yama and travelling the sky. The same yogic sequence of root fire and drunk nectar is a path to siddhi in Tirumular and, in Arunagiri, a step toward loss of the self.

670 says the siddhis come into being when Shakti Tripurai grants grace (திரிபுரை சத்தி அருள்தர). Thiruppugazh 194 says that if one knows Murugan as the gem, everything comes, and that mercury and the metals (இரதாதிகளால்) give only charcoal. Both deny that technique alone yields the powers and give them to a deity's gift, Shakti in one and Murugan in the other.

671 says those who have gained the eight with the Supreme are siddhas because they reach the supreme world (சித்தர் பரலோகஞ் சேர்தலால்). 1674 says the Siva-jnani, being one of silence, is released and a siddha (முத்தனாஞ் சித்தனாம்). Both define the siddha by the goal rather than the powers, and 1674 reaches it by knowledge and silence instead of the eight.

674 says that if the times of dying stay in one's own control (சாகின்ற காலங்கள் தன்வழி நின்றிடின்), great lightness comes in five years. Naladiyar 6 says the appointed days cannot be exceeded and no one has leapt clear of Death. The conflict holds if 674 means control over the hour of one's own death, as its wording suggests.

677 says after seeing the light of the breath (காலொளி) the passing times no longer pass. 680 repeats the last two lines word for word (போகின்ற காலங்கள் போவது மில்லையே) after the light of lightning (மின்னொளி). It is a near-repeat in the chapter, with the light named differently.

677 says that after seeing the breath's light, the passing times do not pass (போகின்ற காலங்கள் போவது மில்லையாம்), playing on கால் as breath and time. Kural 334 says the day is a blade that saws through life (உயிர் ஈரும் வாளது) for those who see it. The conflict holds if 677 means that the master of breath is no longer worn down by time; on a reading where it describes only an inner experience, the claims do not meet.

681 says that for those who know there is nothing that goes, nothing that comes, nothing that dies (போவதொன் றில்லை வருவது தானில்லை சாவதொன் றில்லை). 2854 says that for those who examine the hidden thing there is no going, no coming and no ruin (போக்கொன்றும் இல்லை வரவில்லை கேடில்லை). The near-repeat, in a chapter on powers and a chapter on seeing Siva, puts the knower's changeless state beyond the lights 677 to 680 describe.

682 says that dwelling in Parashakti for a year makes entering another body (பரகாய மேவல்) possible. 2133 uses that power as a simile: the subtle body, after heaven and hell, takes a new birth like a yogi who enters another body (பரகாய யோகிபோல்). The same act is a hard-won siddhi in 682 and, in 2133, what every soul does in rebirth.

686 says the yogi becomes able to create, protect and destroy (தானே படைத்திட ... அளித்திட ... சங்காரத் தலைவனு மாயிடும்), and that it is said of him, he is himself the one. 1809 uses the same தானே refrain for the Lord, who creates, protects, destroys, conceals and himself grants release. 1809 keeps concealment and the granting of release with the Lord, two acts 686 does not give the yogi.

686 gives the yogi who has gained the siddhis the power to create, protect and destroy. 1611 says that for those to whom silence has come the five acts come forward (ஐந் கருமமும் முன்னுமே). Both let the Lord's acts pass in some measure to the perfected one, by siddhi in 686 and by silence in 1611.

688 turns vashitva into being the very self of all lives (உயிர்க்கெல்லாந் தற்பொருளாகிய தன்மையன்). Thiruppugazh 1045 asks for the state in which 'mine' and 'I' fall away and everyone and everything becomes oneself (எவரும் யாதும் யானாகும்). Both make the highest power an identity with all beings rather than control over them.

706 counts escaping death and old age (மரணஞ் சரைவிடல்) among the twenty-one powers. Thiruppugazh 1316 asks whether, fattening the belly with food every day, one can gain the yogic power that lengthens life (உயிரினீடு யோக சித்தி), and seeks instead the feet of knowledge. The song doubts that the indulgent can win the power 706 lists, and sets the feet above it.

707 says circling the world and walking till the feet ache is of no use (பயனில்லை), and those who see the Lord in love know where he dwells. 509 says there are many holy waters within the heart, and those who do not bathe there wander over hollow and height (பள்ளமும் மேடும் பரந்து திரிவரே). Both set the inner place against the pilgrim's road, by love in 707 and by inward bathing in 509.

707 says walking round the world till the feet ache brings no gain (பாதங்கள் நோவ நடந்தும் பயனில்லை). 1445 tells the reader to seek through lands, towns and temples (நாடு நகரமும் நற்றிருக் கோயிலுந் தேடித் திரிந்து), singing and bowing, after which the Lord takes the heart as his temple. The conflict holds if 707's 'no use' is absolute; if it means walking without love, 1445's chariyai is the outward stage that 707 assumes is already passed.

source_issues: 650 and 662: variants are garbled (கோண்-கிய வாமுத்தி; தளண்-களி W\டுபோய்ப்), and 664 (ஓண்-கே), 679 (படையானவையெலாண்-), 705 (சிணண்-குற்ற ... சித்திதாண்-) and 711 (கலந்தெண்-குந்) show the same encoding damage.
693: வேட்டை (hunt) makes little sense; the variant வெட்டை (open space) is likely the better reading.
644: the variant அருமிரு for அருமிகு changes 'four' to possibly 'two'.
666: the variant கூத்தனை நாடுகின்றேனே reverses who seeks whom.
694 to 703: breath counts are given without a key and may be corrupt in places.
